key_insight: In surgically repaired congenital heart disease, true gaps in care are common and are linked to serious preventable complications, often driven by insurance and social instability rather than medical factors.
clinical_relevance: Patients who re-enter care after long gaps may already have progressed disease, and a meaningful fraction need urgent intervention or experience major morbidity or death.
method: Retrospective cohort of 1,746 patients with surgically repaired CHD seen at a tertiary center (2003–2020)
Gaps in care defined as >3 years 3 months between cardiology visits and beyond the recommended follow-up interval
Large-dataset screening was paired with manual chart review to separate true gaps from appropriate care patterns
evidence_signal: After chart review, 275 patients (15.7%) had true gaps in care; 41.5% returned to care, 13% of those required intervention, and 26.7% of intervening cases had serious morbidity or mortality.
watch_item: Single-center retrospective data may limit generalizability, and documentation may undercount social contributors to care gaps.
paper_title: Gaps in Congenital Heart Disease Care: Social Drivers and Clinical Consequences
